module.purpose: Defines the generic state and action contracts used by the React Flow store, including graph data, viewport configuration, interaction settings, event handlers, lookup maps, and imperative mutations.
module.summary: This module is a type-only schema for the React Flow runtime store. It separates persistent graph and interaction state from actions that mutate nodes, edges, viewport constraints, selections, connections, and change middleware, then combines both contracts into the complete store state. The definitions are generic over node and edge types and connect React-facing callbacks with lower-level system primitives.
module.businessContext: Supports an interactive node-and-edge diagram editor. If these contracts drift, rendering, selection, connection, viewport, and graph-editing integrations can fail at compile time or behave inconsistently.
classes: ReactFlowStore (~L54-160): Represents graph data, interaction state, configuration, callbacks, and lookup indexes.
ReactFlowActions (~L162-183): Represents imperative mutations for graph, selection, connection, viewport, and changes.
ReactFlowState (~L185-189): Combines the complete store data contract with its available actions.
systemCapabilities: Apply node and edge change middleware

edgeCases.inputShape: Absent optional callbacks and nullable runtime objects
edgeCases.behavior: The contract permits optional handlers and null values for DOM, pan-zoom, selection rectangle, connection handle, and resolver state.
Fit-view options may be undefined while the resolver is nullable.

edgeCases.inputShape: Optional node and edge arguments for default initialization
edgeCases.behavior: Default node and edge initialization accepts either or both collections as omitted arguments.

invariants.description: The combined store exposes both all state properties and all action operations.
Node and edge state and callbacks remain parameterized by their corresponding generic types.
Lookup maps, connection state, interaction flags, and required configuration fields are represented as present values.

assumptions.description: Generic node and edge arguments satisfy the imported Node and Edge constraints.
Consumers provide implementations for callbacks and action functions represented by the contracts.
The runtime store may use browser DOM elements through the HTMLDivElement field.

ambiguities.question: Which concrete store implementation supplies the declared state and action behavior?
What ordering and middleware semantics apply when change handlers are invoked?

concurrencyModel.notes: This file contains only compile-time type declarations; runtime scheduling and action ordering are defined by implementations elsewhere.
